questions.text:
enum E { A = 1 }
E.A = 9
console.log(E.A)
console.log(E[1])
console.log(E[9])

enum E { A = 0, B = 0 }
console.log(E[0])

const s = "b"
enum E { A = s }
console.log(E.A)
console.log(E["b"])

enum E { A = -1, B }
console.log(E.B)

enum E { A = "a", B = A }
console.log(E.B)

type T = `id-${number}`
const s: T = "id-4"
console.log(s)

type T = 1 extends number ? 2 : 3
const n: T = 2
console.log(n)

const o = { n: 1, m: 2 } as { n: number }
console.log(o.m)

function f<T = number>(x: T) { return x }
console.log(typeof f("a"))

const t = [1] as const
;(t as unknown as number[]).push(2)
console.log(t.length)

class A { constructor(public n = 3) {} }
console.log(new A().n)

class A { constructor(public n?: number) {} }
console.log(new A().n)

const x: { t: "a"; n: number } | { t: "b"; s: string } = { t: "a", n: 5 }
console.log(x.n)

const s = Symbol("a") as unique symbol
console.log(typeof s)

const f: () => void = () => 1
console.log(f())

class A { declare n: number }
console.log(Object.hasOwn(new A(), "n"))

Ничем. В JS остаётся только значение, которое вы сами записали
